draft.title: The end of the Cold War
card: Mikhail Gorbachev became Soviet leader in 1985. The Soviet economy was weak and the arms race was costly, so he tried to reform the system.
openness. It allowed more free speech and criticism of the government.
restructuring. It aimed to make the Soviet economy work better, with some market-style changes.

Gorbachev also would not use Soviet force to keep control in Eastern Europe. In 1989 communist governments fell across the region and the Berlin Wall was opened in November. The Soviet Union broke up in December 1991, and the Cold War was over.
draft.remember: Reform at home and no Soviet force abroad let the Eastern bloc fall, and the Soviet Union itself collapsed in 1991.

a.q: What did Gorbachev's policy of glasnost involve?
opts: More openness and freedom to criticise the government
Restructuring the economy with market-style changes
Building up Soviet nuclear weapons to match the West
Using Soviet troops to keep control of Eastern Europe
a.why: Glasnost means openness, so it allowed more free speech and criticism. Perestroika is the policy of restructuring the economy, so it is the most tempting wrong option, but it is a different policy.
a.clue: Glasnost is about what people were allowed to say.

b.q: Why did communist governments in Eastern Europe fall in 1989?
opts: Gorbachev would not send Soviet force to keep them in power
Soviet troops withdrew after losing a war with NATO
The United States invaded the region and removed them
Gorbachev ordered every communist leader to resign
b.why: Gorbachev would not use Soviet force to keep control, so these governments could not rely on Moscow to prop them up. The Cold War ended without a direct war between the superpowers, so a defeat by NATO is wrong.
b.clue: Think about what Gorbachev refused to do in Eastern Europe.

a.best: More openness and freedom to criticise the government

b.best: Gorbachev would not send Soviet force to keep them in power
